## Checked and left as is

- Segment counts: `l` agrees with `t` word by word except where one Geʿez word has been written as two English words (ዘ- "what/that" + verb, እንዘ ይብል "saying"), as in ch. 70/71; I did not hyphenate these, since the published parts do not. Proclitics ወ- ለ- በ- እም- ከመ are hyphenated throughout.
- Heading ፸፪ = ሰብዓ ወክልኤ; ፲ወ፰ (18) ዐሠርቱ ወሰመንቱ and ፲ወ፬ (14) ዐሠርቱ ወአርባዕቱ agree with the house entries; ዓሥሩ ወክልኤ (12) is written out in the text.
- `p` flags: units 1 and 2 only (heading; the one paragraph). Longest unit is 17 at 44 words (no ፤ to cut at, source has none between እስከ ለዓለም and ወሶበ); every unit ends at ። ፤ ፨.
- Parses I checked and found right: ኮነት, ሐነጸ, ረሰዩ, ተወልደ, ነግሠ, ለአከ, ወሀበ, ሤመ, ባረከ, ቀብአ, አምሐለ, አዘዘ, በጽሐ, ተፈሥሐ, ሐተተ, ከልሐ, አኀዘ, ተዋቀሰ; ዘ- relatives; ኢታስተአክዩኒ (2mp, root hedged); ዘኣነግሥ (1cs imperfect, ነ); ኢያምልክ (jussive); ይቀንእ; ለእመ + perfect.
- House renderings kept: "king-of Rome", "tribe" (ነገድ), "mounted/mule-of king", "younger" for ዘይንእስ (ch. 70), "kinsman"; Sheol not in this part.
- Names: l keeps Bezold's three spellings of Baltasar's name in the notes; l writes "Baltasor", i "Baltasar" throughout (ch. 70/71 have no precedent). Adrami / Ardamis, Zänbäres (i "Zenberes"), Akimihel, Adlonia, Arsani, Yodad: not identifiable, kept as spelled, noted as unidentified.
- Vineyard-riddle ending: a unit-by-unit comparison of l against t for 40–54 found no dropped word. ቈጽል (leaf), አዕጹቅ (branches), ሥርው (root), ጒንድ (stock), አሕሩግ (runners; the plural form is confirmed by ሠረዋ አሕሩገ ጒንዲ in the next chapter's first words) and ቆዕ (flowering part) are the five terms; ቆዕ stays "tendril (?)". The verdict itself lies in ch. 73, so "breaks off before the verdict" in `about` is right and "first case" is borne out by that chapter's heading.
- `about`: left unchanged ("eldest daughter" follows ትልህቅ; flagged (?) in the unit 38 note).

## Refused findings

- Hyphenating ዘ- everywhere in `l` ("what-we-heard"): ch. 70/71 mix both ways and a mass change would not improve accuracy; I only touched l where the parse was wrong.
- Retyping or re-splitting any `t` (forbidden); the ፨ inside units 32, 35, 37, 39 end the units where Bezold prints them.
- Changing "Zenberes" i-form or standardising Baltasar/Baltasor: no house rule; the notes name the variant spellings.
- Rendering ነሥኡ (unit 24) as a flat past in `i`: no reading is clearly best (imperative impossible by the vowelling; a perfect of certainty/purpose reads oddly before ወሀቡ), so I kept the drafter's "Let the people of Israel take" and recorded the doubt in n; listed as unresolved.
- Replacing "tendril" for ቆዕ with "blossoming shoot" or similar: no evidence beyond the next chapter's ጽጌ ቆዕ "blossom of ቆዕ"; kept the drafter's (?) guess.
- Dropping the "Genesis 10 / Hosea 2:23 / 1 Peter 2:10 / 1 Kings 1:33" allusions: they are named as "compare", not asserted.
- Re-reading ወልዲ as "my son" to follow the existing glossary entry: the third-person narration (units 11, 29, 37) needs "his"; the conflict is recorded in the unit 11 note for the glosser (broaden the entry, do not change it).
- Reading ነጋሢ as plural: refused (the reverse was the fix): ነጋሢ is the singular agent noun; plural is ነገሥት.

## For the glosser / pass 2 (not touched: only units.json and review.md edited)

- ፫: entry gives ሠለስቱ; before አዋልድ the spoken form is probably ሠለስ (the entry already has this as (?)).
- ወልዲ: existing entry "my son"; here "his son" (-ዲ for -ዱ).
- አውሥአ: lemma root ወሥአ (matches the entry); do not spell ወሰአ.
- ነጋሢ: singular "king" (existing entry fine).
- የዐብያ: 3fp imperfect of ዐበየ, not a causative; አስተአከየ, አስተፋነወ, አጽዐነ (from ጸዐነ/ጽዕነ), ይቴሐቱ, መላህቅት, መንእሳነ need hedged lemmas; በልዓ (unit 52) 3fp perfect or በልዐ + -ā (?); ዘኣነግሥ imperfect (not jussive).
